dedupe_keys.name: hourly wind and solar generation profiles at 1 8th degree resolution contiguous us 1980 2099

description: This data set simulates hourly wind and solar power generation on a 1/8 degree grid across the contiguous United States, for historical and future climates. It was published in 2023 by Cameron Bracken, Travis Thurber and Nathalie Voisin in the GODEEEP project, with code in the tgw-gen repository and profiles produced with NREL's reV model. The aim is to give generation profiles at new sites or where records are short, and to study climate change impacts on renewables. A generic plant is assumed in every grid cell, with solar at the surface and wind at 80, 100 and 125 m hub heights, driven by regional climate model output from the TGW data set. Periods are historical 1980 to 2022 and future 2020 to 2099 under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5, each in hotter and cooler variants. Values are capacity factors that can be scaled to any plant size. Coverage is the contiguous US. Files are NetCDF, one per year, grouped by resource, scenario and year range into linked Zenodo records, downloadable under CC0 at no cost. Caveats: the profiles use generic plants, not actual fleets, and the index record holds only a README. Simulation uses are capacity expansion and climate adaptation studies. Related records: data-eia-2020-plant-wind-solar-hourly-profiles gives plant-level profiles from the same group.
